class_id: a hand-typed coverage list (writers, readers, caches, tables) is checked against nothing, so it drifts from the code it claims to cover
feature: any guard whose reach is a list a person typed: which writers honour a flag, which readers a cache invalidation covers, which tables a trigger protects, which routes a filter wraps
symptom: a guard is built as a list of the places it applies to. The list is right on the day it is written and wrong the first time the code grows or the list is typed from memory: a new writer never asks, a table is listed under a column it does not have, a cache key is missing. Nothing compares the list to the code, so the gap is found only by a reviewer reading both, or by production. Universal shape: coverage by enumeration without a check that the enumeration is complete and correct. The fix is to invert it: ONE predicate that every site must call, plus a static test that fails when any site outside the predicate reads the underlying fact, and a runtime check that derives the population from the system's own catalog.
